claims.explanation: MG-132 is a proteasome inhibitor, so selective killing likely reflects a high proteotoxic load and dependence on proteasome/ubiquitin-mediated turnover, often driven by activated RTK/RAS/PI3K signaling or FBXW7 loss. Constitutive NF-kB and HIF-1alpha activity further sensitize because MG-132 blocks IκB degradation and stabilizes HIF-1alpha. The provided most/least lists overlap for several lines, so these features are proposed as testable predictors rather than definitive from the screen alone.

features.basis: PI3K/AKT/mTOR activation increases protein synthesis and proteasome load
Loss of E3 ligase causes oncoprotein accumulation and proteotoxic stress
RTK-driven protein synthesis increases proteasome dependency
MAPK activation increases protein synthesis and proteotoxic load
Constitutive NF-kB activity creates dependence; MG-132 blocks IκB degradation
MG-132 stabilizes HIF-1alpha; excessive HIF-1 activity can induce apoptosis
Annotated target; high proteasome subunit expression may indicate proteasome addiction
DNA repair defect may sensitize to proteasome inhibitor-induced stress
VHL loss increases HIF-1alpha, which MG-132 further stabilizes
MYC-driven protein synthesis increases proteasome load; virtual cell shows downregulation of MYC target genes
Virtual cell upregulation and NF-kB dependence
BAG3 is anti-apoptotic and facilitates proteasome degradation; high baseline may confer resistance
